title: AXIN Solution built to meet Norwegian weighing compliance deadlines
summary: New regulations are reshaping how Norway's seafood industry receives wild-caught fish. From January 1, 2027, operators receiving wild-caught pelagic fish must have automatic scales and automatic weighing system (AWS) in place. Wild-caught whitefish operators face the same requirement one year later, from January 1, 2028.
body_markdown:
The regulations, introduced by the Norwegian Ministry of Trade, Industry, and Fisheries, are designed to strengthen traceability across the fish supply chain and give authorities better visibility into what is actually being caught and landed.


To help processors meet these requirements as smoothly and as cost-effectively as possible, JBT Marel worked directly with the Norwegian Directorate of Fisheries to develop the[AXIN Fish Receiving Process Solution](https://jbtmarel.com/en/products/axin-fish-receiving-process-solution/) ; a purpose-built compliance solution for controlled intake registration, certified weighing data capture, traceability, audit trail management, and automatic compliance reporting to The Directorate of Fisheries.


#### Understanding the regulation


Announced in early 2026, the new rule requires recipients of wild-caught pelagic fish to use a certified automatic scale and weighing system that ensures all fish received are weighed accurately, with the necessary data stored and electronically transferred to the Directorate of Fisheries at each landing. Weighing and event data must remain accessible for at least five years to support inspections.


Beyond simply recording weight, the regulation requires that weighing data be linked to key identifiers, including the landing location, fish species, details of the receiving operation, and associated weighing activity. The AWS itself must be able to exchange electronic data with fish sales organizations’ ticket systems (the final delivery note) and other downstream systems relying on the weighing results. It must also include a built-in function to flag, correct, and resubmit data in the event of errors or gaps in what has been transmitted.


The regulation’s core purpose is straightforward: establish consistent, verifiable weighing standards for pelagic fish starting in 2027, and extend the same requirements to whitefish operators in 2028, closing gaps in traceability across the sector. The[full regulatory text is available via Lovdata](https://lovdata.no/dokument/LTI/forskrift/2026-02-03-130) .
